recipes.name: Great Grilled Smoky Vegetables with Avocado and Goat Cheese Crumbles
ingredients_raw: 4 red bell peppers, cored and quartered
1 pinch cayenne pepper, or to taste
freshly ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Place mushrooms, red bell peppers, and red onion in a 9x13-inch baking dish. Whisk olive oil, lime juice, grill seasoning, garlic, and cayenne pepper in a small bowl; pour over vegetables. Toss to coat and allow vegetables to marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat grill for medium heat and lightly oil the grate.
Remove vegetables from the marinade, and shake off excess. Reserve remaining marinade.

Grill vegetables on preheated grill until tender, about 5 minutes. Transfer grilled vegetables to a large platter. Whisk remaining marinade with balsamic vinegar; pour over vegetables. Top with avocado and goat cheese, then season with salt and pepper. Sprinkle with basil to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Great Grilled Smoky Vegetables with Avocado and Goat Cheese Crumbles
raw_recipe.description: Marinated mushrooms, bell peppers, and onion are grilled, then served with creamy white goat cheese and luscious avocado in this versatile side dish.

review.reviewBody: You MUST make these!! They are awesome and will impress everyone. My picky in-laws (but I don't like goat cheese..) loved them, my 13 year-old son (mom, when can we have those grilled vegetables again?...). Very easy to substitute depending on what veggies you have on hand. Have made this 5 times, here are my suggestions: slice the onion THICK or they will get lost. add zucchini (quartered lengthwise) and/or asparagus, eggplant is good also. MOST IMPORTANT: PUT SOME BALSAMIC IN YOUR MARINADE, THEN ADD GOOD/HIGH QUALITY BALSAMIC TO SOME OF THE REMAINING MARINADE TO DRIZZLE ON THE GRILLED VEGGIES. The avacado is optional but the goat cheese and FRESH basil are a must. Addistional suggestion: on the chance that you have leftover veggies, cut them up and add to sauteed onion and garlic, throw in a can of diced tomatoes and some grilled, sliced chicken sausage. Simmer to desired consistancy and serve over pasta with additional cheese. I now make extra veggies every time, just so we can have the pasta. Did I mention I like this receipe :)

As soon as I saw this recipe, I knew I had to try it. Love veggies, love grilling, love goat cheese, love avocado. I made this a few nights ago, and It. Was. Awesome! Following reviewers' advice, I put about a tablespoon of the balsamic into the marinade. I let it all sit for about 90 minutes, and I ended up grilling everything for about 10 min. As another reviewer suggested, I then put the veggies into a 300-degree oven while I was finishing the main course.

Another reviewer described making extras and stirring them into a pasta meal with sauteed onions and garlic and chicken sausage. I did exactly what she described and served with more goat cheese crumbles. (Parmesan would have been good, too, but I didn't have any.) Again, fabulous. We have just enough veggies and sausage left to stir into scrambled eggs or omelettes this weekend!

I've made a lot of great recipes off this site, but this may be my favorite. It's pretty much foolproof, it's versatile, and it's delicious. And I'm no great chef or anything.

This was EXCELLENT! I am not a great cook and made this to take to an EASTER dinner. Takes a while to cut up the veges otherwise it's easy. I cut the red peppers into 6ths instead of quarters so it was easier to serve. EVERYONE GOBBLED IT UP and asked for the recipe. Thanks EVERYONE who made suggestions! I added 1 large zucchini and 2 small yellow Squashes like many people said. Grilling was out of the question that day, so I too roasted the veges in the oven 20 minutes on 400 then I had to set to Low broil as they seemed to be cooking slowly. (may have just been my Samsung Oven.) This made enough for 9 people. I doubled the marinade since I had 2 pans marinating but honestly that was too much marinade and had plenty of that left over of that. I did not use any over it after it cooked. It didn't need it. I will definitely make this a GO-TO recipe.

Such a versatile recipe! I used green, red and yellow bell peppers, sliced zucchini, sliced baby bella mushrooms, asparagus, red onion, and quartered roma tomatoes. I marinated everything in a large ziploc bag instead of a dish. That way I could easily mix it and flip it periodically. I skipped the avocado, and sprinkled a few little gobs of goat cheese at the end. I totally forgot using the basil, but will try next time even though it wasn't needing it. This is a keeper recipe for roasting or grilling veggies that I will use over and over. Thanks so much for sharing it. :-)

I put these on the BBQ in a vegetable basket and they were truly smoky! I left them on longer than 5 minutes until tender and periodically stirred them. Instead of the red pepper I used a green one and added asparagus, zucchini, and summer squash.

The best veggies! I too accidentally added the BV to the marinade and don’t regret it. Was too cold to grill so did these in the oven to perfection. The add ins of fresh basil and avocado really made it. And goat cheese. That’s the reason I chose this recipe!

I took others suggestions and also added asparagus and also sliced zucchini. I also add the balsamic vinegar to the entire marinade instead of whisking it and adding it after grilling. Every time I serve this everyone loves it! It is a summertime hit.

Absolutely amazing! Like another said, I'm dreaming of the next time I have this! I made the recipe exactly as above except I mistakenly added the balsamic vinegar while marinating instead of after grilling - but it was so good I don't think I'd try it the original way. 
We used the suggested ingredients, plus zucchini (quartered lengthwise), yellow bell pepper, and eggplant sliced into 1/2" rounds, all good. The red onion is a must, it is a wonderful flavor complement to the other veggies. My suggestion, make a lot, especially if you're feeding more than 3 or 4 people - it'll be a hit.

Added lime zest and the balsamic vinegar at the beginning, used only 1 tablespoon of EVOO, then marinated veggies and cut up chicken (in separate ziplock bags) for 6 hrs. Made my own all purpose seasoning as I didn't have grill seasoning. Followed rest of recipe. Grilled like kabobs for 10 mins, it was delicious.

This is an incredible recipe! I used zucchini, yellow squash, green & red pepers, red onion and asparagus. As some had suggested .. I used fresh basil and included the balsamic vinegar in the marinade. Sooo yummy!

I made it few times when we were hosting friends and everyone like it. I omitted grill seasoning (too salty for me) and added brussel sprouts just because I wanted my husband to start eating them. He did, and now it became a fixed ingredient in that dish. Eventually more veggies made it's way to this dish... i.e when I had some left over zucchini and didn't want to waste it, a potato after I peeled too many and decided to slice the excess to add to this dish. I also mix the peppers, some red, some yellow or orange and green ones too. I did that for more colorful look of the dish, and because we like them all. You can use frozen peppers if you don't have fresh ones. We love this recipe, and the offshoot I created. If you decide to go with the extras, grill/bake potatoes and brussel sprouts for 10 minutes before adding other ingredients. They take longer to get soft. This recipe + steak + bottle of good vine is an official start of dining outside season. Thank you for sharing!!
This stuff is fantastic! Our favorite recipe and we follow it as is!
I didn't try it but it sounds great! I only "rated" it in order to get my question answered - what's "grill seasoning " consist of?
Our family's favorite! We eat these all summer long!

SO, so good! ANY vege will work with this recipe for grilling. We used a mix of bell peppers, red onion, poblano, asparagus and mushrooms. The second shot of marinade is the key! It gives it lots more flavor. Subbed Feta for Goat cheese and it was amazing. Didn't have avocado but I'm sure that would have made it super amazing.
I like to add zucchini to this and sometimes other seasonal grilling veg, but that’s about the only change I make to the recipe.

I not only made it once, but I made it three times within a two week period! My family and friends loved it and the presentation actually made it look like I was a great chef! Looks very impressive and tastes great too!

FABULOUS!!!!! Will make it again and again! My whole family gobbled it up! I followed the recipe but also added zucchini. The goat cheese and avocado, along with the smokiness of the grilled veggies, made it phenomenal!
Incredible grilled veggies! Didn't change a thing.

I’ve made this dozens of times over the past few years - some times with all of the ingredients and some times not. I generally leave out the avacado and goat cheese because I rarely have them in the house. I especially like this marinade with portobello mushrooms. When my wife is gone I kick up the cayenne to spice it up a bit. Delish!
